print.summary: Writes each value to standard output without appending a newline.
print.details: Values use Oryn's default representation. Strings are written without quotes; arrays and algebraic values include their delimiters.

parameters.values: Zero or more values to format and write, in argument order.

print.returns: `Unit` after all values have been written.

println.summary: Writes each value to standard output and terminates the line.
println.details: Formatting is identical to `print`. Exactly one newline is emitted after the final argument, including when no arguments are provided.

parameters.values: Zero or more values to format and write, in argument order.

println.returns: `Unit` after the line has been written.

assert.summary: Checks that a condition is true and stops the program when it is false.
assert.details: Use assertions for invariants and programmer errors. They are not a replacement for `Option` or `Result` when failure is expected during normal execution.

parameters.condition: Boolean expression that must evaluate to `true`.

assert.panics: Panics with `assertion failed` when the condition is false. A non-boolean argument produces an `expected Bool` runtime error.

panic.summary: Immediately terminates the program with a fatal error message.
panic.details: Use `panic` only when execution cannot safely continue. Recoverable failures should be represented with `Option` or `Result`.

parameters.message: Human-readable explanation of the fatal error.

panic.panics: Always. Passing a non-string value also produces a runtime panic.

len.summary: Returns the length of an array or string.
len.details: For arrays, the result is the number of elements. For strings, the current runtime reports the number of UTF-8 bytes, not Unicode code points or grapheme clusters.

parameters.value: Array or string whose length will be measured.

len.panics: Panics when `value` is neither an `Array` nor a `String`.

get.summary: Retrieves an array element without allowing an out-of-bounds access.
get.details: Indices start at zero. Negative indices and indices greater than or equal to the array length return `None`.

parameters.values: Array to read from. The array is not modified.
parameters.index: Zero-based position of the requested element.

get.panics: Panics when the first argument is not an array or the index is not an `Int`.

Some.summary: Constructs an `Option` that contains a value.
Some.details: Use `Some` when a computation successfully produced an optional value. Consume it with `match` rather than assuming a value is present.

None.summary: Represents an optional value that is absent.
None.details: `None` carries no payload. Safe lookup operations return it when no element exists.
examples: match value { Some(x) => println(x), None => println("missing") };

Ok.details: Use `Ok` for an operation that completed successfully and produced a value.

parameters.value: Successful value stored in the result.

Err.details: Use `Err` for expected failures that callers can inspect and handle. Fatal invariants should use `panic` instead.

parameters.error: Error value describing why the operation failed.

len.summary: Returns the length of an array or string.
len.details: Array length counts elements. String length currently counts UTF-8 bytes rather than Unicode code points or grapheme clusters.
len.panics: Panics when the receiver is neither an `Array` nor a `String`.

is_empty.summary: Tests whether an array or string has a length of zero.
is_empty.details: Equivalent to `value.len() == 0`. The receiver is not modified.
is_empty.returns: `true` when the receiver is empty; otherwise `false`.
is_empty.panics: Panics when the receiver is neither an `Array` nor a `String`.

get.summary: Retrieves an array element with bounds checking.
get.details: Indices start at zero. This method makes lookup failure explicit instead of causing an unsafe memory access.

parameters.index: Zero-based position of the requested element.

get.returns: `Some(value)` for a valid index; otherwise `None`, including for negative indices.
get.panics: Panics when the receiver is not an array or `index` is not an `Int`.

first.summary: Returns the first element of an array, if one exists.
first.details: The array is not modified. This is equivalent to a safe lookup at index zero.
first.panics: Panics when the receiver is not an array.

last.summary: Returns the last element of an array, if one exists.
last.details: The array is not modified. Empty arrays are handled explicitly with `None`.
last.panics: Panics when the receiver is not an array.

contains.summary: Tests whether a string contains a contiguous fragment.
contains.details: Matching is case-sensitive and byte-based. An empty fragment is considered present.
contains.returns: `true` when the fragment occurs in the receiver; otherwise `false`.
contains.panics: Panics when either the receiver or `fragment` is not a `String`.

starts_with.summary: Tests whether a string begins with a prefix.
starts_with.details: Matching is case-sensitive and byte-based. Every string starts with the empty string.

parameters.prefix: Prefix to compare with the beginning of the receiver.

starts_with.returns: `true` when the receiver starts with `prefix`; otherwise `false`.
starts_with.panics: Panics when either the receiver or `prefix` is not a `String`.

ends_with.summary: Tests whether a string ends with a suffix.
ends_with.details: Matching is case-sensitive and byte-based. Every string ends with the empty string.

parameters.suffix: Suffix to compare with the end of the receiver.

ends_with.returns: `true` when the receiver ends with `suffix`; otherwise `false`.
ends_with.panics: Panics when either the receiver or `suffix` is not a `String`.

map.summary: Transforms every array element and returns the collected results.
map.details: The transform runs once per element in source order. The source array is not modified, and evaluation is eager.

parameters.transform: One-parameter anonymous function that produces a new value for each element.

map.returns: A new array containing the transformed values.
map.panics: Panics at runtime if the receiver is not an array or the argument is not a function.

filter.summary: Returns the elements accepted by a predicate.
filter.details: Elements retain their original order. The source array is not modified, and evaluation is eager.
filter.returns: A new array containing only elements for which the predicate returned `true`.
filter.panics: Panics at runtime if the receiver is not an array or the argument is not a function.

fold.signature: array.fold(initial: A, combine: fn(A, T) -> A) -> A
fold.summary: Reduces an array from left to right into one accumulated value.
fold.details: The initial value is returned unchanged for an empty array. Evaluation is eager and follows source order.

parameters.combine: Two-parameter anonymous function receiving the accumulator and current element.

fold.returns: The final accumulator after every element has been processed.
fold.panics: Panics at runtime if the receiver is not an array or `combine` is not a function.
examples: [1, 2, 3].fold(0, fn(acc: Int, n: Int) => acc + n); // 6
